chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah, both, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about a man, is it permissible for him to pray on a shelf suspended between two palm trees? He said: 'If it is level and he is able to pray on it, there is no harm.'

And I asked him about a silk bedspread and similar to it from dibbaj (silk brocade), and a silk prayer mat and similar to it from dibbaj, is it permissible for a man to sleep on it, lean on it, and pray on it? He said: 'He spreads it out and stands on it, but he does not prostrate on it.'

And I asked him about a man who prays in a mosque whose walls are all facing the qibla, and its sides, and his wife prays opposite him, he sees her and she does not see him? He said: 'There is no harm.'
And I asked him about the prayer mats (bawari) whose reeds are moistened with dirty water, is one allowed to pray on them? He said: 'When they dry out, there is no harm.'

And I asked him about a man who prays with him is a leather pouch of donkey skin and he is wearing shoes of donkey skin, does his prayer suffice or does he have to repeat it? He said: 'It is not permissible for him to pray with it being with him unless he fears it will be lost, then there is no harm in him praying with it being with him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for praying on silk, brocade, and with donkey skin items present?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarates the fiqh of prayer spaces and materials, emphasizing that permissibility often hinges on the absence of impurity (najāsah) or specific prohibitions rather than mere location. It notably distinguishes between using silk for sleeping and prostrating, and allows for minor impurities on prayer mats once dry, reflecting the Shia principle of conditional purity. The ruling on donkey skin highlights the practical consideration of preserving the item if its removal might cause loss, showcasing the juristic balance between ritual purity and practical necessity.
